t: The Cimmerians were culturally and archaeologically indistinguishable from the Scythians, yet every source of their own time treated them as a separate people.
After crossing the Caucasus they defeated Urartu, destroyed the empire of Phrygia, sacked Sardis and for a time ended Neo-Assyrian control in Anatolia, helping the Medes and Lydians rise.
Around c. 635 BC the Scythians under Madyes and the Lydians under Alyattes defeated them, and they disappeared from history, assimilated by the peoples of Anatolia.
dyk: By 657 BC an Assyrian astrologer was calling the Cimmerian king Dugdammî šar-kiššati, 'King of the Universe', a title normally held only by the king of Assyria and given to no other foreign ruler in the empire's history.
ev: The Cimmerians help Colchis and nearby regions defeat attacks by Urartu
The Cimmerians heavily defeat Rusa I of Urartu, in the first recorded mention of them
Esarhaddon kills the Cimmerian king Teušpâ in a campaign in Cilicia
Under Dugdammî the western Cimmerians destroy the empire of Phrygia and sack Gordion
Gyges of Lydia defeats the Cimmerians and sends captured city-lords to Ashurbanipal
The Cimmerians and Treres capture Sardis except its citadel, and Gyges is killed
Dugdammî falls gravely ill on campaign and takes his own life in Cilicia
Scythians under Madyes and Lydians under Alyattes defeat the Cimmerians and Treres

f.homeland: the Caspian and Ciscaucasian steppes north of the Caspian Sea, between the Araxes (Volga) and the Cimmerian Bosporus (Kerch Strait), in present-day Southern Russia; later māt Gamir around Gori in Georgia, then Cappadocia and Central Anatolia, with a capital at Ḫarzallē, and an eastern group near Mannai and Media
f.period: part of the Chernogorovka-Novocherkassk complex (9th to mid-7th centuries BC); in Transcaucasia from c. 750 BC; first recorded in 714 BC; division into western and eastern groups under Esarhaddon (681–669 BC); the height of power under Dugdammî, called 'King of the Universe' by 657 BC; final defeat around c. 635 BC
f.known: mounted archery with Scythian-type socketed arrowheads and sigmoid bows; the defeat of Rusa I of Urartu; the sack of Gordion and the fall of Phrygia; the sack of Sardis in 644 BC and the death of Gyges; the destruction of the Artemision of Ephesus; Animal Style art; bringing trousers to Central Europe
f.sources: no written records of their own; Neo-Assyrian records of the 8th to 7th centuries BC (intelligence reports, oracle texts, royal inscriptions); Graeco-Roman authors from Homer and Herodotus to Strabo; the Hebrew Bible as Gōmer; kurgans, weapons and horse gear from the steppe, Caucasia and Anatolia; genetic studies of 2018 and 2019
